sa→C Overview and Quick Start

sa build-c compiles an SA program into a single-file, auditable C99 program (implementation: sci/src/emit_c.zig, built with Zig 0.17). The design goal is safe, auditable C: deterministic output, no hidden dependencies, zero warnings under gcc -Wall -Wextra, combined with Gas metering and linear-memory bounds checks, which suits embedding SA programs in scenarios with static-checking requirements on C code, such as checkout rules and audit pipelines.

1. Basic Usage

sa build-c demos/c/01_hello_world/main.sa -o sa_program.c --project-root .
cc -Wall -Wextra -std=c99 -O2 sa_program.c -o sa_program
./sa_program   # hello, saasm
  • --project-root is used for package resolution (sa_std imports and .sa_cache).
  • The output is a single .c file: a header comment identifies the generator, followed in order by includes/types, linear memory, sa_trap, Gas, the on-demand runtime helpers, const definitions, function forward declarations, function bodies, an (optional) indirect dispatch table, and main.
  • The complete output for hello_world is about 43 lines, containing only the four runtime symbols sa_trap + sa_gas + sa_addr + sa_print_bytes.

Notesa→C emits an executable program (containing int main), not a library: export/test functions that are never called are trimmed away; #npm_bind is still JS-only, and on the C side npm-family externs are replaced by native staged implementations (see the extern Host Bindings (Staged Simulation) page).
